```{r}
#| label: setup
#| include: false

# ---- Packages ---------------------------------------------------------------
# Loaded once here so that the analytical sections below contain only
# analytical code. Versions are reported in the reproducibility appendix.
suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(sf)                 # vector geospatial data and CRS handling
  library(dplyr); library(tidyr); library(purrr); library(stringr)
  library(lubridate)          # local-time handling
  library(ggplot2); library(patchwork); library(scales)
  library(ggspatial); library(ggrepel); library(forcats)
  library(terra)              # raster covariates
  library(spatstat.geom)      # ppp / owin / im classes
  library(spatstat.explore)   # KDE, K, G, F, J, rhohat, envelopes
  library(spatstat.model)     # ppm, kppm
  library(spatstat.random)    # rpoispp and other null-model simulators
  library(sparr)              # spatio-temporal kernel density
  library(gt)                 # tables
})

source("R/utils.R")

sf::sf_use_s2(FALSE)   # planar predicates: all analysis happens in EPSG:32749
set.seed(1234)         # every Monte-Carlo result below is reproducible

# ---- Load the prepared objects ---------------------------------------------
# Built by scripts/03_prepare.R .. scripts/07_valueadded.R. Each script is
# reproduced and explained in the corresponding section of this report.
DER      <- "data/derived"
P        <- readRDS(file.path(DER, "params.rds"))
audit    <- readRDS(file.path(DER, "qa_audit.rds"))
dup_rep  <- readRDS(file.path(DER, "dup_report.rds"))
persist  <- readRDS(file.path(DER, "persistent_pixels.rds"))
bnd      <- readRDS(file.path(DER, "bnd_proj.rds"))
kec      <- readRDS(file.path(DER, "fo_kecamatan.rds"))
win      <- readRDS(file.path(DER, "win.rds"))
fire_sf  <- readRDS(file.path(DER, "fire_sf.rds"))
fire_all <- readRDS(file.path(DER, "fire_all_sf.rds"))
fire_px  <- readRDS(file.path(DER, "fire_pxday_sf.rds"))
fire_ev  <- readRDS(file.path(DER, "fire_event.rds"))
ppp_det  <- readRDS(file.path(DER, "ppp_det.rds"))
ppp_px   <- readRDS(file.path(DER, "ppp_pxday.rds"))
ppp_ev   <- readRDS(file.path(DER, "ppp_event.rds"))
covars   <- readRDS(file.path(DER, "covars.rds"))
osm      <- readRDS(file.path(DER, "osm_clipped.rds"))

FO_T   <- readRDS(file.path(DER, "fo_temporal.rds"))
FO_Q   <- readRDS(file.path(DER, "fo_quadrat.rds"))
FO_K   <- readRDS(file.path(DER, "fo_kde.rds"))
FO_R   <- readRDS(file.path(DER, "fo_rhohat.rds"))
FO_C   <- readRDS(file.path(DER, "fo_covsummary.rds"))
FO_ST  <- readRDS(file.path(DER, "fo_stkde.rds"))
SO <- tryCatch(readRDS(file.path(DER, "so_results.rds")), error = function(e) NULL)
VA <- tryCatch(readRDS(file.path(DER, "va_results.rds")), error = function(e) NULL)

# ---- Quantities used repeatedly in the prose -------------------------------
AREA_KM2 <- area(win) / 1e6
N_DET    <- npoints(ppp_det)
N_PX     <- npoints(ppp_px)
N_EV     <- npoints(ppp_ev)
DATE_MIN <- min(fire_sf$date_local)
DATE_MAX <- max(fire_sf$date_local)
N_DAYS   <- as.integer(DATE_MAX - DATE_MIN) + 1L
LAM_BAR  <- N_PX / AREA_KM2

# Geodesic (ellipsoidal) area of the study window, used in Section 2 as the
# reference against which the projected area's distortion is measured. s2 is
# switched on only for this one calculation, then switched back off, because
# every other spatial predicate in the report is planar by design.
sf::sf_use_s2(TRUE)
AREA_GEOD <- as.numeric(sf::st_area(sf::st_transform(bnd, 4326))) / 1e6
sf::sf_use_s2(FALSE)
CRS_ERR_PCT <- 100 * abs(AREA_KM2 - AREA_GEOD) / AREA_GEOD
```

## <span class="en">Abstract</span><span class="zh">摘要</span> {#sec-abstract .unnumbered}

::: {.en}
Pulang Pisau Regency holds much of the drainage network left behind by
Indonesia's abandoned Mega Rice Project, and it burns in almost every dry
season. This report treats 3,101 VIIRS 375 m active-fire detections, recorded
inside the regency between 4 and 11 September 2026, as one realisation of a
spatial and spatio-temporal point process.

Detection intensity varies about fortyfold across the regency. It rises
sharply close to engineered canals and falls close to natural rivers. The two
effects keep opposite signs after multivariate adjustment, and that is what
separates a drainage mechanism from simple proximity to water.

The second-order analysis is built around a sequence of null models, and its
main result is methodological. A homogeneous Poisson null is rejected, but the
rejection carries no information. A kernel-based inhomogeneous Poisson null
then gives *opposite answers* at different intensity bandwidths. It is not
rejected at 1–2 km. At 10 km it is rejected decisively. We read this as a
problem of identifiability and statistical power, not as a finding about fire.
The p-value falls monotonically as the null becomes less flexible, so the
verdict is tracking the model and not the data. Replacing the kernel with a
parsimonious parametric null breaks the impasse. A covariate-driven Poisson
process is rejected. A Thomas cluster process carrying the same trend is not,
and it estimates compact clusters of roughly 2.1 km.

A Monte-Carlo Knox test on permuted dates then establishes genuine space-time
interaction, using no bandwidth and no covariates at all. Throughout, the
analysis keeps the behaviour of the fire field separate from the behaviour of
the satellite. That distinction accounts for most of the apparent day-to-day
variation.
:::

::: {.zh}
Pulang Pisau 县境内保留着印尼「百万公顷稻米工程」遗留的大片排水渠网,几乎每个
旱季都会过火。本报告把 2026 年 9 月 4 日至 11 日该县记录到的 3,101 个
VIIRS 375 m 活跃火点探测,视为一次空间与时空点过程的实现加以分析。

一阶分析显示,探测强度在全县范围内相差约四十倍。它在**人工运河**附近明显升高,
在天然河流附近反而降低。两者的方向在多变量调整之后依然相反,正是这一点把
**排水机制**与泛泛的「靠水」区分开来。

二阶分析围绕一组逐层放宽的零模型展开,其主要结果属于**方法学**层面。齐次泊松
零模型被拒绝,但这一拒绝不提供任何信息。改用基于核的非齐次泊松零模型之后,不同的
强度带宽给出了**相反的答案**:在 1–2 km 下不被拒绝,在 10 km 下被决定性地拒绝。
我们把它判断为**可识别性与检验力**的问题,而不是关于火本身的发现。随着零模型变得
不那么灵活,p 值单调下降,说明判定追踪的是模型而不是数据。把核估计换成一个简约的
参数化零模型可以打破僵局。由协变量驱动的泊松过程被拒绝;带有同一趋势项的 Thomas
聚集过程没有被拒绝,并估计出约 2.1 km 的紧凑簇群。

随后,在置换日期上进行的蒙特卡洛 Knox 检验确立了真实的时空交互,整个过程既不使用
带宽,也不使用任何协变量。全篇始终把火场的行为与卫星的行为分开来看。这一区分
解释了逐日表观变化中的大部分。
:::
